F10-01: Questions ask for horizontal/vertical distances, perimeters and areas read from plotted points; the pupil reads coordinates from the grid, which is the skill. The concealed view is the native board with the helper text only (no measurements).
F10-02: Image coordinates are asked as "x, y" (answerType coordinates). Source vertices are visible by design; questions were chosen so no answer coordinate appears in the source labels or evidence panel.
F10-03: Midpoint and distance answers use decimals or values off the axis labels; reading the end points is the skill. Concealed view shows the line only.
F10-04: Table values are given; the hidden column is the plotted point set. Native step renderer forces its own preset, so Guided phases use a custom call into the same scene function.
F10-05: Hosts all four F6-08 presets (Y7-060, Y8-035, Y8-036, Y9-020) natively; Challenge rounds 1-4 are those F6-08 rounds. Engine patch: the task-0 caption now prints the lesson's own gradient (native always printed y = −x + c). Proportion presets force c = 0 in the contract. F6-08 hosting is also checked by a dedicated host test (test-f6-08-host.cjs).
F10-06: Gradient is read from two marked points on the grid; rise and run are hidden until marking. The concealed caption with A and B coordinates shows in a standalone mount, but the template game hides the helper-strip caption, so in the game the pupil reads A and B from the grid (all at whole-number grid points). Rounds 1-3 (and 4-5) share the same visible text and differ only in the plotted points; the 'each round shows its own apparatus' check therefore counts drawn SVG geometry as well as text.
F10-07: Parallel/perpendicular gradients are asked from the given line; the comparison line is not drawn in the concealed view.
F10-08: Intersections are asked as "x, y" (coordinates). Reading the crossing from the graph is the skill, so an accurate drawing necessarily shows it; the numeric evidence panel is hidden.
F10-09: Real-life graph readings; the graph must be visible to read. The native geometry is fixed at load from matchMedia (760 px); relayout replays the draw, covered by the resize suite.
F10-10: Distance-time speeds and stops; reading the graph is the skill. Round titles come from the lesson title field. Geometry fixed at load from matchMedia (760 px), replayed on relayout.
F10-11: Speed-time accelerations and distances (area); reading the graph is the skill. Geometry fixed at load from matchMedia, replayed on relayout.
F10-12: Quadratic turning points/roots/values; the curve is visible, so roots can be read from the graph (the skill). Numeric evidence hidden until marking.
F10-13: Cubic/reciprocal/exponential values at stated x; the curve is visible. Expected text uses the native equation labels.
F10-14: Transformation answers: turning point as "x, y" or y at a stated x. The equation is shown (it is the given); turning point, symmetry, roots and intercept readouts are hidden.
F10-15: Yes/no membership of a test point. The concealed view draws the boundary only (no shading). Engine patches: inequality text now uses the sign of the constant (native printed y ≤ −x − 2 for y ≤ −x + 2), and the test-point verdict is hidden in an unmarked Challenge.
F10-16: Radius is read from the grid (r = ? in the concealed view); questions ask for diameter, area or circumference. Two rounds share a preset with different radii, so 5 of 6 rounds have distinct text (the drawing differs in all 6).
F10-17: Choice answers (A, B or C). The answer letter is necessarily one of the visible graph labels, so concealment is checked as: no matched, focused or selected graph and no proof text. Lessons choose a preset only. Engine patch: the focus trail receives path data (native passed an SVG group and logged an SVG error on every draw).
F10-18: Piecewise readings use half-step x values; open/closed endpoint questions ask for "a, b" (ordered). Engine patch: segment trail receives path data (native logged an SVG error on every draw).
F10-19: Trig values to 2 d.p., max/min as "a, b", and tan 90° = undefined (text). Engine patch: the asymptote note is hidden in an unmarked Challenge (it gave away "undefined").
F10-20: Tangent gradients, trapezium estimates and over/under (text). The native scene had no draw hook, so it is recorded for relayout via the build's rec list. Engine patch: the over/under note is hidden in an unmarked Challenge. Area and over/under questions use revealed phase 9/12 so their revealed views show the trapezia (phase 5 showed only the tangent and made two views identical).
